---
title: "Styling a Quarto Website with CSS and SCSS"
---

## Why styling matters

A consistent visual system improves readability, navigation, and credibility. This portfolio uses a custom CSS file in addition to Quarto's built-in Cosmo theme.

## CSS in this website

CSS controls the appearance of HTML elements. The site's `_quarto.yml` contains `css: styles.css`, which loads our custom stylesheet across pages.

```css
.hero {
  padding: 2rem;
  background: #f4f0e9;
  border-radius: 16px;
}
```

The `.hero` class is used on the home page to create a distinct introductory section.

## How SCSS extends CSS

SCSS supports reusable variables, nesting, and mixins. For example, a shared color variable helps maintain consistent styling:

```scss
$accent: #567c82;

.hero {
  border-left: 5px solid $accent;
  h2 { color: $accent; }
}
```

The sample is provided in `examples.scss` to demonstrate SCSS syntax. The live site currently uses compiled-style plain CSS from `styles.css`.

## Design decisions

- A neutral background supports readability.
- Teal accents create a consistent visual hierarchy.
- Responsive spacing makes the site easier to use on smaller screens.
- Clear navigation labels help visitors find portfolio work quickly.
